blocks.text: 🏮 Our Kyoto Adventure — 3 Days
Ten thousand orange gates, wild monkeys, a golden temple and a real steam train — here's the plan, day by day.

items.title: Fushimi Inari Shrine
items.note: Beat the crowds! Hike under thousands of torii gates — the higher you climb, the quieter it gets. Fox statues everywhere: count them!

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.note: 'Kyoto's Kitchen' — graze your way down the arcade: tamagoyaki skewers, mochi, fresh juices. Everyone picks their own snack.

items.title: Kamo River Stroll
items.note: Easy walk along the water as the light fades. Herons, stepping stones, and a perfect end to a big walking day.

items.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
items.note: Walk through towering green stalks that creak in the wind — go early for the magic (and photos without strangers).

items.title: Monkey Park Iwatayama
items.note: A short uphill hike earns you wild monkeys roaming free and a panorama over all of Kyoto. Kids' highlight!

items.title: Tea House Stop
items.note: Slow down with matcha and sweets — grown-ups get calm, kids get wagashi treats.

items.title: Ramen Night
items.note: Steaming bowls for everyone. Slurping is polite — family slurping contest encouraged.

items.title: Kinkaku-ji — the Golden Pavilion
items.note: A temple covered in real gold leaf, mirrored in its pond. Straight out of a storybook.

items.title: Ryoan-ji Rock Garden
items.note: 15 stones, but you can never see all 15 at once from any spot. Family challenge: who can count the most?

items.title: Kyoto Railway Museum
items.note: The kids' reward: real locomotives to climb aboard, and a working steam train ride. Allow a good couple of hours.

items.title: Farewell Izakaya
items.note: One last feast of small plates — yakitori, gyoza, rice balls. Toast the trip with juice and tea all around.

blocks.title: Getting around
blocks.text: Day 1 is all on foot — comfy shoes on! Days 2 and 3 we ride the bus: grab an IC card (ICOCA) so everyone can tap on and off without fumbling for coins.

items.title: Fushimi Inari Taisha
items.note: Go early to beat the crowds. The full torii-gate loop to the summit takes ~2–3h; turn back at Yotsutsuji viewpoint for the city panorama if short on time.

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.note: Lunch as a grazing walk: tako tamago, soy-milk doughnuts, fresh sashimi skewers. ~400m covered arcade, budget 1.5–2h.

items.title: Teramachi & Kawaramachi stroll
items.note: Optional wind-down: shops and cafés a few minutes' walk from Nishiki.

items.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
items.note: Arrive before 9 for the quiet, photogenic path. 20–30 min walk-through.

items.title: Tenryu-ji Temple & garden
items.note: UNESCO-listed Zen temple; the pond garden borrows the Arashiyama hills as scenery.

items.title: Lunch by the river
items.note: Yudofu (tofu hot pot) is the local specialty; riverside restaurants along the Katsura.

items.title: Togetsukyo Bridge & riverside
items.note: Cross the bridge, then optionally climb to Iwatayama Monkey Park (~20 min uphill) for the view over Kyoto.

items.title: Kinkaku-ji
items.note: Opens 9:00 sharp — be at the gate for the gold pavilion mirrored in the pond with fewest people. One-way garden loop, ~1h.

items.title: Ryoan-ji rock garden
items.note: Optional add-on: famous Zen rock garden, a short bus ride or 20-min walk away.

items.title: Matcha & souvenir stop
items.note: Matcha soft-serve and wagashi along the temple approach before heading out.

blocks.title: Getting around
blocks.text: Day 1: JR Nara Line to Inari Station (2 stops from Kyoto Station), then subway/bus to Nishiki. Day 2: JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama (~15 min). Day 3: bus 101 or 205 from Kyoto Station (~40 min). Get an IC card (ICOCA/Suica) for tap-and-go on all of it.

blocks.text: Kyoto with the Family · 3 Days
Torii gates, bamboo forests, monkeys, gold temples and a lot of noodles — here's our adventure, day by day.

groups.label: Day 1 · On foot — gates, snacks & river light

items.title: Fushimi Inari
items.note: Beat the crowds! Thousands of orange torii gates to wander through — fox statues everywhere. Kids: count the foxes!

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.note: "Kyoto's kitchen" — graze your way down the covered street: skewers, mochi, tamagoyaki. Everyone picks their own snack.

items.title: Kamo River stroll
items.note: Easy riverside walk as the light goes golden. Herons, stepping stones, and people-watching on the banks.

groups.label: Day 2 · By bus — bamboo, monkeys & ramen

items.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
items.note: Walk through towering green stalks that creak in the wind — go early for the quiet magic.

items.title: Monkey Park
items.note: A hilltop climb with a payoff: wild monkeys roaming free and the whole city at your feet. Feeding happens inside the hut!

items.title: Tea house stop
items.note: Slow down with matcha and sweets — a calm reset for little legs (and big ones).

items.title: Ramen night
items.note: Steaming bowls all around. Slurping is encouraged — it's polite!

groups.label: Day 3 · By bus — gold, rocks & trains

items.title: Kinkaku-ji
items.note: The Golden Pavilion — a temple covered in real gold leaf, mirrored in its pond. Postcard moment.

items.title: Ryoan-ji rock garden
items.note: 15 rocks, but you can never see them all at once from any spot. Family challenge: who can count the most?

items.title: Kyoto Railway Museum
items.note: The kids' pick! Real steam locomotives, train simulators, and a giant layout. Allow plenty of time.

items.title: Farewell izakaya
items.note: One last feast of little plates — yakitori, gyoza, rice — and a toast to a great trip. Kanpai!

blocks.title: Getting around
blocks.text: Day 1: we walk everywhere — comfy shoes on! Days 2 & 3: hop the city bus. Board at the back, pay when you get off, and grab an IC card so nobody has to fish for coins.

blocks.text: Kyoto · 3 Days

items.title: Fushimi Inari Taisha
items.note: Go at sunrise — the thousand torii gates are nearly empty and the light is best. Full summit loop is ~2–3h; the Yotsutsuji viewpoint (~45 min up) is the sweet spot if you want to save legs.

items.title: Train back to central Kyoto
items.note: Inari Station is right at the shrine gate; ~5 min to Kyoto Station.

items.title: Nishiki Market lunch crawl
items.note: Graze the 'Kyoto's Kitchen' lane: tamagoyaki, soy-milk doughnuts, tako tamago, fresh sashimi skewers. Most stalls wind down by 17:00–18:00.

items.title: Teramachi & Shinkyogoku arcades
items.note: Covered shopping streets — knives, tea, sweets, souvenirs. Easy stroll after eating.

items.title: Dinner in Pontocho
items.place: Pontocho Alley, along the Kamo River
items.note: Lantern-lit narrow alley of restaurants; riverside terrace seating in warm months.

items.title: Bamboo Grove
items.note: Arrive before 8:00 — by 9:30 it's a queue, not a grove. 10-minute walk but worth lingering.

items.title: Tenryu-ji Temple
items.note: UNESCO-listed; the Sogenchi garden borrows the Arashiyama hills as scenery. Opens 8:30.

items.title: Okochi Sanso Villa
items.note: Quiet hillside garden with matcha included in the ticket — the antidote to the grove crowds.

items.title: Togetsukyo Bridge & riverside
items.note: The 'moon-crossing' bridge; grab lunch nearby — yudofu (simmered tofu) is the local specialty.

items.title: Iwatayama Monkey Park
items.note: Wild macaques plus the best panorama over Kyoto. Skip if legs are tired from Day 1's climb.

items.title: Sagano Romantic Train (optional)
items.note: Scenic gorge ride — book seats ahead in autumn. Otherwise, coffee along the river and an early night.

items.title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
items.note: Opens 9:00 — be at the gate on time; the gold leaf mirrored in Kyoko-chi pond is the classic shot, best in morning light. The grounds loop takes ~45–60 min.

items.title: Matcha & sweet at the tea house
items.note: Small tea garden near the exit — matcha with a wagashi, seated overlooking the pond.

items.title: Ryoan-ji rock garden
items.place: 15-min walk or short bus ride away
items.note: Fifteen stones, and you can never see all fifteen at once from the veranda. Pairs naturally with Kinkaku-ji.

items.title: Ninnaji or Kitano Tenmangu
items.note: Ninnaji for a five-story pagoda and palace halls; Kitano Tenmangu if it's the 25th (monthly flea market).

items.title: Last souvenirs & departure
items.note: Station's Isetan basement and Porta mall for last-minute sweets (matcha KitKats, yatsuhashi) before your train.

blocks.title: Make the early starts count
blocks.text: All three headliners — the torii gates, the bamboo grove, the Golden Pavilion — are transformed by arriving before the crowds. Get an IC card (ICOCA/Suica) for buses and trains; buses cover Kinkaku-ji's northwest corner best, trains are faster for Fushimi Inari and Arashiyama.

blocks.text: Kyoto with the Family · 3 Days
Torii gates, bamboo forests, monkeys, golden temples and a lot of good noodles. Here's the plan — read it together and pick your favourite moment!

groups.label: Day 1 · On Foot — Gates, Snacks & River Light

items.title: Fushimi Inari Shrine
items.note: Beat the crowds! Thousands of orange torii gates tunnel up the mountain — it feels like walking through another world. Fox statues everywhere: count them as you climb.

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.note: "Kyoto's Kitchen" — a long covered street of snack stalls. Everyone picks their own treats: tamago skewers, mochi, fresh fruit. Grazing lunch, family style.

items.title: Kamo River Stroll
items.note: A slow walk along the water as the light turns gold. Herons, stepping stones, and plenty of space for the kids to run. The perfect easy end to a big walking day.

groups.label: Day 2 · By Bus — Bamboo, Monkeys & Ramen

items.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
items.note: Towering green stalks that creak and sway overhead. Go early for the quiet magic — and look straight up for the best photo of the trip.

items.title: Iwatayama Monkey Park
items.note: A hilltop climb with a big reward: wild monkeys roaming free and all of Kyoto spread out below. The kids can feed them from inside the hut — the monkeys come to you!

items.title: Tea House Stop
items.note: Slow down with matcha and sweets in a traditional tea house. Grown-ups get calm; kids get something green and sweet. Everyone wins.

items.title: Ramen Night
items.note: Steaming bowls, slurping encouraged. Let everyone order their own — miso, shoyu, or extra chashu for the hungry ones.

groups.label: Day 3 · By Bus — Gold, Rocks & Trains

items.title: Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion
items.note: A temple covered in real gold leaf, mirrored in its pond. Straight out of a storybook — best in morning light.

items.title: Ryoan-ji Rock Garden
items.note: Fifteen stones in raked gravel — but you can never see all fifteen at once from any spot. A puzzle for the whole family: can anyone find the trick?

items.title: Kyoto Railway Museum
items.note: The kids' grand finale: real steam locomotives, train simulators, and a giant layout. Hands-on fun after two days of temples.

items.title: Farewell Izakaya
items.note: A lively Japanese pub-dinner: lots of small plates to share, everyone tries something new. Toast the trip — kanpai!

blocks.title: Getting around
blocks.text: Day 1 is all on foot — comfy shoes are the secret weapon. Days 2 and 3 ride the bus: grab an IC card (ICOCA) so everyone can tap on and off without fumbling for coins. Kids will love watching the flat fare go in.

blocks.text: Kyoto in 3 days

items.title: Fushimi Inari Taisha
items.note: Go early to beat the crowds. The full loop through the torii gates to the summit takes ~2–3 hours; turn back at Yotsutsuji viewpoint if short on time.

items.title: Train to downtown
items.note: ~30–40 min to the Nishiki area.

items.title: Nishiki Market
items.note: Graze your way through: tamagoyaki, soy-milk doughnuts, grilled seafood skewers. Most stalls wind down by late afternoon.

items.title: Stroll Teramachi & Shinkyōgoku
items.note: Covered shopping streets — an easy afternoon wander, tea stops and knife shops.

items.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
items.note: Arrive before 8 for the grove nearly to yourself.

items.title: Tenryū-ji
items.note: UNESCO-listed Zen temple; the Sōgenchi pond garden is the highlight.

items.title: Togetsukyō Bridge & riverside
items.note: Classic view of the bridge with the mountains behind.

items.title: Lunch in Arashiyama
items.note: Yudōfu (simmered tofu) is the local specialty.

items.title: Iwatayama Monkey Park
items.note: Optional — wild macaques plus a panorama over Kyoto. Skip if legs are tired.

items.title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
items.note: Opens 9:00. Morning light on the gold leaf over the mirror pond is the best photo of the trip.

items.title: Garden loop & tea house
items.note: One-way path through the strolling gardens; matcha and a sweet at the tea garden.

items.title: Lunch nearby / head back
items.place: bus or taxi to central Kyoto
items.note: Kinkaku-ji is a half-day stop — keep the afternoon free for souvenirs or a revisit to a favourite spot.

blocks.title: Getting around
blocks.text: Grab an IC card (ICOCA/Suica) for trains and buses. Day 1 pairs naturally — Fushimi Inari is south, Nishiki downtown; Arashiyama deserves the whole of Day 2; Kinkaku-ji is a morning trip, so Day 3 stays relaxed.
